exposure: prenatal exposure to ambient air pollution
outcome: gene expression changes in nasal cells
cohort: 700 Danish children were followed clinically for the development of asthma and allergy, with air pollution exposure modeled from conception to 6 years of age.
finding: Higher prenatal exposure to NO2, PM2.5, and PM10 was associated with an altered nasal mucosal immune profile at 4 weeks, an increased odds of allergic sensitization and allergic rhinitis at age 6 years, and an altered immune profile in blood at 6 months, conferring increased risk of asthma at age 6 years.
